# Host reference for the teleop lock, recorded 2026-07-28 on x86_64
# GNU/Linux, gcc 13, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, -ffp-contract=off.

# This file locks THIS HOST against itself across refactors. It is NOT a
# cross-architecture claim — baselines/host-x86_64.txt is the file that
# makes that one. trace_fnv1a covers every frame's target pose, engaged
# flag and qpos; the sampled trace lines exist so a failing diff points
# at the first frame that moved.
#
# The trace value below was recorded BEFORE any of this landing's
# commits, by compiling the then-current app/teleop.cc against a
# throwaway xr_shell.h stub, with app/main.cc:149-183 replicated inline.
# Every commit since has had to reproduce it — including the multi-robot
# landing, which renamed this file from teleop-host-x86_64.txt, moved the
# scene to build/franka/, and rewrote nine things in src/ik_dls.{h,c}
# without moving the hash by one bit.
#
# TWO FIELDS HERE ARE NOT BITWISE, and they are the only two compared off
# this architecture (the trace comparison is skipped, loudly, elsewhere):
#   opt_*        the scene's solver configuration, so a wrapper XML that
#                silently loses its <option> block fails as a named line.
#   pos_med_mm   median target-to-TCP distance over the engaged frames,
#                compared with a 1.5x + 1 mm tolerance. 23.69 mm here is
#                not a defect: this robot's clutch_scale is 1.0 against
#                the SO101's 0.5, so the script commands it twice as far
#                and twice as fast. See ReachWatch in bench/teleop_replay.cc.
#
# REGENERATE WITH:
#   ./build/teleop_replay build/franka/ar_scene.xml \
#       > baselines/teleop-franka-host-x86_64.txt
# then RESTORE THIS COMMENT BLOCK BY HAND — teleop_replay does not emit it,
# so a plain redirect silently deletes the provenance above. Regenerating is
# a deliberate, separately argued act: trace_fnv1a is a bitwise lock, so a
# diff means the dynamics moved, and the question is why rather than how to
# make it green again.
# teleop replay: scripted engage/move/release/recenter/reset
